Some organizations may not have project charter and other related information readily available. In these situations, business and technology stakeholders should conduct overall project scoping discussions prior to performing this task.

The purpose of this task is:

  • To obtain stakeholder agreement on scope of the test effort
  • To determine appropriate test coverage for the target solution
  • To establish a framework that guides the test effort

Element.attribute: Engage stakeholders to identify risks, define scope and address project constraints
Engage stakeholders to identify risks, define scope and address project constraints

Engaging experienced business and technology stakeholders is key to identifying risks in the target solution and defining scope for the test effort. Mitigating risk in the target solution is one of the main reasons to perform testing. Stakeholders define the scope of the test effort with the intent to mitigate key risks in the target solution. Stakeholders should be involved, to build and provide a clear plan that mitigate risks and a contingency plan in case of risk realization. Proper scope definition includes defining not only in-scope, but also out-of-scope areas for the test effort. Areas of scope may include business processes and systems, as well as IT systems and other technology components. Prioritization of risks and components in the target solution may be needed for successful completion of the test effort within stipulated timelines and budget.

Key test related constraints and dependencies are also identified. Constraints and dependencies may impact the way in which certain aspects of the target solution are tested and the timing of the test. Discuss these risks and constraints with stakeholders and devise a plan to address these throughout the test lifecycle.

Element.attribute: Define test levels and types to test the target solution
Define test levels and types to test the target solution

Structuring the test effort into levels and types encourages a systematic approach that instills a level of confidence in stakeholders that appropriate coverage is provided and risk mitigation in the target solution is improved. Test levels define the target of the test (the whole system, certain components, etc.) while test types define the purpose or objective of the tests performed. For each test level defined, identify the components of the target solution under test and the type of tests performed at each level. Since each test type represents a test objective, the intent is for the test types defined in each level to mitigate a risk in the target solution.

Defining the necessary test levels with stakeholders is usually accomplished at this stage in the test effort. An initial list of test types performed at each level may be defined, however, further refinement of test types and how test objectives are fulfilled is expected when defining a test approach for each test level.

Element.attribute:
Discuss with business and technology stakeholders a strategy for providing appropriate coverage for environment and data needs. Topics to address include:

  • Number of required environments (e.g., one environment for each test type or one environment for multiple test types?)
  • Number of users each environment needs to support (e.g., how many users can login into one environment at one time?)
  • Security access needed for users (e.g., read-only or read-write permissions for environment users?)
  • Separate environments for third party involvement in the test effort

Element.attribute: Using a testing tool to support activities in the test effort is a common practice. Testing tools typically have features that support and automate a number of activities in the test lifecycle, including creation of test cases, test execution automation, code monitoring, data generation, defect management, test result analysis, coverage monitoring and status reporting. Test management tools are influential in reducing costs, increasing efficiencies, streamlining processes and coordinating tasks among test resources. Making a decision to use and to select a test management tool should be discussed with stakeholders.

Discuss with stakeholders a strategy for obtaining and managing test data. A primary consideration for obtaining test data is whether to use generated or production data. Other considerations to discuss include:

  • Defining a process to request and obtain test data
  • Defining how test data is copied into test environments

Element.attribute: Define test metrics and status reporting
Define test metrics and status reporting

Discuss with stakeholders how to track the progress of the test effort throughout the project lifecycle. The goal is to define testing metrics and reporting so that stakeholders are aware of what is available for reporting and what testing metrics are expected and required, at a minimum, to successfully complete testing cycles. Perform the following:

  • Determine the reporting frequency (e.g., daily, bi-weekly, weekly)
  • Determine what information will be reported on (e.g., (a) number of defects created, resolved and closed (b) number of scripts started, attempted, completed, successful, failed)
  • Determine what tools will be used and who will create the reports
  • Determine what is the acceptable exit criteria to move out of a test cycle (e.g., How many defects can remain open, % of scripts pass/fail)
  • Determine what is the acceptable status for go-live. (e.g., can any defects be open, can any scripts be incomplete or failed?)
